summary: What the extraction cannot know, for Noria. Six townspeople, and nothing else yet: the placement list came out clean, its heights agree with the heightmap at a median of nought, and MU's own checkpoint on the attribute grid passes. See tests/worlds.py, and docs/porting-a-world.md.

spawns.lift_why: She hovers. ZzzCharacter.cpp's MONSTER_ELF_LALA arm ends `o->Position[2] = RequestTerrainHeight(o->Position[0], o->Position[1]) + 140.f`, which is a metre and forty above the tile - she is a winged fairy and MU lifts her rather than animating a hover. She is the only character in 0.75 that does this, and a spawn table that carries a tile and a facing has nowhere else to say it.

spawns_from: OpenMU's Version075/Maps/Noria.cs, CreateNpcSpawns, which is six lines:
CreateMonsterSpawn(1, NpcDictionary[253], 169, 109, Direction.SouthEast)
CreateMonsterSpawn(2, NpcDictionary[253], 193, 110, Direction.South)
CreateMonsterSpawn(3, NpcDictionary[242], 173, 125, Direction.SouthWest)
CreateMonsterSpawn(4, NpcDictionary[243], 195, 124, Direction.South)
CreateMonsterSpawn(5, NpcDictionary[240], 172,  96, Direction.SouthEast)
CreateMonsterSpawn(6, NpcDictionary[238], 180, 103, Direction.SouthWest)
The numbers are the same ones the client switches on, and which model each becomes
is ZzzCharacter.cpp's own: 253 is MODEL_MERCHANT_GIRL, 242 MODEL_ELF_WIZARD, 243
MODEL_ELF_MERCHANT, 240 MODEL_STORAGE and 238 MODEL_MIX_NPC. Three of those five had
no asset in this project before Noria, because three of them stand nowhere else.
Two of Lorencia's nine turn up here as well and are the same people rather than
copies: Amy keeps a second shop in the elf town and Baz a second vault. Elf Lala and
Eo the Craftsman are Noria's alone, which is why Folk's note said 0.75 has neither
*in Lorencia* - they were never missing, they were somewhere nobody could go.
The facing is the same (facing - 3) * 45 the town's is, pinned against Lorencia's
campfire once and linear in the direction value, so it needs no second landmark.
No guard carries an idle here, where six of Lorencia's do. Noria has no guards: its
six are all PassiveNpc in OpenMU's own initialisation, and the idle on a Lorencia
guard is a fact about a player model in or out of a safe zone, which none of these
is.
